summary: WhatsApp session keys and user activity exfiltrated to author-controlled MongoDB and Telegram
details: The package is a WhatsApp/Baileys bot that, at startup, connects to a hardcoded MongoDB Atlas cluster at `unity-free.pc6vkvw.mongodb.net` (credentials `unity-free:unity-free` shipped in `config.env` and `config/index.js`) and persists Baileys auth state — WhatsApp credentials and signal/noise keys — via `useMongoDBAuthState` into an `AuthState` collection on that author-controlled database. Any operator who pairs a phone with the bot hands full WhatsApp session control (equivalent to a hijacked account) to the author. Message-reaction handlers and dashboard/boost notifications additionally POST to `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage` with a hardcoded `chat_id` of `7752365037`, silently relaying reacting users' phone numbers and event/message content to the author's Telegram account. The shipped `config.env` also contains live third-party credentials (Google Gemini API key, two Telegram bot tokens, a Gmail SMTP app password). On successful pairing, `autoFollowChannels` invokes `sock.followNewsletter` on hardcoded author-owned WhatsApp newsletter JIDs (e.g. `120363419201971095@newsletter`) and a cron re-runs every 6 hours to defeat unfollows, using the paired user's WhatsApp identity to boost the author's channels.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
